exam.title: Associate Cloud Engineer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; Google recommends at least six months of hands-on Google Cloud experience. Practice hierarchy, policy, billing, quotas, identity and federation; compute, GKE, Cloud Run and event deployments; storage/data/network selection; Terraform; monitoring, diagnosis, backup/restore, rollout/rollback and least-privilege workload access using both console and command-line tools.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Setting up a cloud solution environment (~20%)
Planning and implementing a cloud solution (~30%)
Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution (~30%)

review.notes: All four current 20/30/30/20 domains and detailed PDF considerations are mapped through foundation, implementation, operation, recovery and least-privilege decisions, with three scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks. All nine guide URLs are cataloged: eight reachable and O'Reilly automation-blocked; none missing or broken. The older five-domain outline and legacy Cloud Functions/Vertex naming are explicitly reconciled with the current branding-update baseline. No proprietary course material, question bank or recalled exam item is used.

findings.title: Lifecycle observation lacked an accepted baseline
findings.evidence: Objective digest unchanged while prior lifecycle snapshot was absent; live page provides separate standard, renewal-exam and designated-learning routes.
findings.recommendation: Initialize only the reviewed missing lifecycle snapshot, retain all three observations and explain separate validity/eligibility routes.
findings.resolution: Initialize only the reviewed missing lifecycle snapshot, retain all three observations and explain separate validity/eligibility routes.

findings.title: Standalone organizations require explicit eligibility and ownership teaching
findings.evidence: Current route is for new Free Trial customers; Organization Owner is outside IAM and distinct from Organization Administrator.
findings.recommendation: Add eligibility, remaining active Google owner, service-account exclusion and delegated-creation boundaries.
findings.resolution: Add eligibility, remaining active Google owner, service-account exclusion and delegated-creation boundaries.

findings.title: Budget types have different enforcement boundaries
findings.evidence: Alerts-only budgets differ from preview single-project/single-service monthly spend caps; estimated trigger can lag and ongoing charges remain.
findings.recommendation: Replace blanket budget claim with explicit budget type, eligibility, delay and manual-lift behavior.
findings.resolution: Replace blanket budget claim with explicit budget type, eligibility, delay and manual-lift behavior.

findings.title: Maximum instances is not a strict dependency budget
findings.evidence: Service-level versus revision-level settings and temporary excess behavior are documented.
findings.recommendation: Teach pool limits, headroom, overlap and observability; local180/228 connection examples are fictional scenarios rather than platform predictions.
findings.resolution: Teach pool limits, headroom, overlap and observability; local180/228 connection examples are fictional scenarios rather than platform predictions.

findings.title: Workload access and image pulls use different identity paths
findings.evidence: GKE federation supports direct workload principals or optional service-account impersonation; node identity still pulls images. Shared pools can identify matching namespaces/accounts as the same principal.
findings.recommendation: Explain identity provenance and separate troubleshooting/negative cases.
findings.resolution: Explain identity provenance and separate troubleshooting/negative cases.

findings.title: Service-account attachment is not token creation or target access
findings.evidence: Service Account User supports actAs; Token Creator supports short-lived token impersonation; target permissions are distinct.
findings.recommendation: Add role/permission table and ADC provenance checks instead of granting broad access to hide wrong credentials.
findings.resolution: Add role/permission table and ADC provenance checks instead of granting broad access to hide wrong credentials.

findings.title: Priority is evaluated within policy order
findings.evidence: Hierarchical/system policies precede configurable classic versus network ordering; terminating actions stop evaluation and goto_next delegates.
findings.recommendation: Replace a flattened priority interpretation with layer/order/target/direction evaluation.
findings.resolution: Replace a flattened priority interpretation with layer/order/target/direction evaluation.

findings.title: New sinks do not backfill historical entries
findings.evidence: Sinks independently evaluate new entries; intercepting aggregated sinks change child routing with a Required exception.
findings.recommendation: Teach storage versus routing, missing history and explicit copy/permission verification.
findings.resolution: Teach storage versus routing, missing history and explicit copy/permission verification.

findings.title: ACL migration can remove access and becomes irreversible
findings.evidence: Uniform access disables ACL authorization and cannot be reversed after90consecutive days; federation access requires it.
findings.recommendation: Teach least-privilege migration, reversal constraints and separate retention behavior.
findings.resolution: Teach least-privilege migration, reversal constraints and separate retention behavior.

findings.title: Delivery guarantees do not establish once-only business effects
findings.evidence: Supported pull/regional/message-ID guarantees do not cover push execution or publish-side duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add transaction/dedup/outbox reasoning and execute a local rollback/retry exercise with explicit distributed-runtime limits.
findings.resolution: Add transaction/dedup/outbox reasoning and execute a local rollback/retry exercise with explicit distributed-runtime limits.

findings.title: Snapshot completion is not application recovery proof
findings.evidence: Pending writes, disk/OS consistency support and operation-versus-resource states differ.
findings.recommendation: Require restore evidence and distinguish Persistent Disk guest coordination from Hyperdisk manual coordination.
findings.resolution: Require restore evidence and distinguish Persistent Disk guest coordination from Hyperdisk manual coordination.

findings.title: Small results and zero estimates do not prove low query cost
findings.evidence: LIMIT on non-clustered data does not reduce scans, clustered estimates may be high and row-level security can return zero estimates.
findings.recommendation: Explain on-demand bytes controls and a negative query-budget case.
findings.resolution: Explain on-demand bytes controls and a negative query-budget case.

findings.title: Old course registry wording needs current deployment mapping
findings.evidence: Container Registry write shutdown does not invalidate gcr.io endpoints backed by Artifact Registry.
findings.recommendation: Preserve catalog evidence and direct new labs to Artifact Registry without claiming every gcr.io image is broken.
findings.resolution: Preserve catalog evidence and direct new labs to Artifact Registry without claiming every gcr.io image is broken.

findings.title: Developer environments need explicit persistence and update boundaries
findings.evidence: Workstations clusters/configurations/instances differ; ephemeral runtime disappears on stop and config updates apply on restart.
findings.recommendation: Add operations teaching and a proposed restart/persistent-home verification case.
findings.resolution: Add operations teaching and a proposed restart/persistent-home verification case.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.

SQLite in-memory transaction checks prove local duplicate/payload/rollback behavior only. No process crash, disk durability, concurrency, outbox dispatcher, external recipient or end-to-end delivery tested.
